text: The Picard-Lindelöf theorem guarantees a unique local solution of the IVP y' = f(x, y), y(x₀) = y₀ provided f is continuous and, as a function of y, is:
explanation: The book's hypothesis is that f is Lipschitz in y, |f(x, y₁) − f(x, y₂)| ≤ K|y₁ − y₂|, which makes the Picard iteration T a contraction so the Banach fixed-point theorem applies. Continuity or boundedness alone gives existence but can fail uniqueness (e.g. f = y^{1/3} is continuous, not Lipschitz at 0, and uniqueness breaks down).
